title: Base-changed system over a chosen stage
statement:
Let $I$ be a directed poset, let $(S_\lambda)_{\lambda\in I}$ be an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with transition morphisms $s_{\lambda\mu}:S_\mu\to S_\lambda$ for $\lambda\leq\mu$, and let $S$ with projections $p_\lambda:S\to S_\lambda$ be a limit $S=\varprojlim_{\lambda\in I}S_\lambda$ of this system (such a limit is assumed given; it exists, e.g., when all transition morphisms are affine, Stacks Tag 01YX, which is the setting of every citer). Fix $\lambda_0\in I$ and a scheme $Y_{\lambda_0}$ equipped with a morphism $Y_{\lambda_0}\to S_{\lambda_0}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. On the subsystem $I_{\lambda_0}=\{\lambda\in I\mid\lambda_0\leq\lambda\}$, define

$$
Y_\lambda=Y_{\lambda_0}\times_{S_{\lambda_0}}S_\lambda,\qquad
Y=Y_{\lambda_0}\times_{S_{\lambda_0}}S.
$$

Here the maps $S_\lambda\to S_{\lambda_0}$ and $S\to S_{\lambda_0}$ are $s_{\lambda_0\lambda}$ and $p_{\lambda_0}$. For $\lambda\leq\mu$ in $I_{\lambda_0}$, define the transition morphism $Y_\mu\to Y_\lambda$ to be the unique morphism induced by $\mathrm{id}_{Y_{\lambda_0}}$ and $s_{\lambda\mu}$ through the fibre-product universal property; define $Y\to Y_\lambda$ similarly using $\mathrm{id}_{Y_{\lambda_0}}$ and $p_\lambda$. (Elementary remarks: $I_{\lambda_0}$ is directed and cofinal in $I$, since any $\lambda,\mu\in I$ have a common upper bound with $\lambda_0$ by directedness; by uniqueness in the universal property the transition morphisms compose correctly and are compatible with the maps $Y\to Y_\lambda$, so $(Y_\lambda)_{\lambda\in I_{\lambda_0}}$ is an inverse system over $Y_{\lambda_0}$. Facts such as $Y=\varprojlim Y_\lambda$ or affineness of its transitions are not part of this definition and must be cited by a user.)
